atAGlance: Mực chiên giòn is crispy fried squid, usually with tender rings or pieces, golden coating, and lime-pepper salt dip or ginger fish sauce.
whatItIs: Mực chiên giòn is crispy fried squid, usually served hot with lime-pepper salt, chili, or a light dip. The outside should crackle before the squid turns chewy.
howToEnjoy: Eat it hot before the coating softens. Dip lightly so the squid stays crisp and does not turn salty.
howLocalsOrder: Order mực chiên giòn as a shared snack or seafood plate. Ask for no chili or extra lime-pepper salt before the plate arrives.
worthKnowing: Vietnamese seafood shops often judge fried squid by timing: crisp coating, tender squid, and no rubbery chew.

travelerCaution: Contains or may contain seafood or shellfish.
